answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying each new account to an attestation chain: to earn standing, an agent must collect endorsements from distant, unrelated attestors spread across the network, not from a tight cluster it controls. Each endorsement locks a small deposit that only unlocks after the endorsed agent behaves well for a long season, so a fable told by one fake to another buys nothing. A gale of fresh accounts therefore faces a lagoon of slow, costly trust that no single operator can flood in parallel.
